newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Im loan for U.S.-China deal said suspended.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Im loan for U.S.-China deal said suspended.

text.p: The United States said Tuesday it was suspending an Export-Import Bank loan to an U.S. company in a deal with a Chinese company that was sanctioned for selling arms-related chemicals to Iran.
State Department Nicholas Burns would not reveal the name of the American firm but said the Chinese company was Nanjing Chemical Industries Group.
"We have decided to suspend the Ex-Im loan that would have supported the export of equipment to the Nanjing Chemicals Industries Group," Burns told reporters.
"We have done so because this company is sanctioned as of May 21. Therefore it would be entirely inconsistent with our non-proliferation policy were we to proceed with an Ex-Im Bank loan," he said.
The transfers involved chemicals and other technology that could be used in chemical weapons.

In the May 21 decision, the United States imposed sanctions on two Chinese companies -- Nanjing and Jiangsu Yongli Engineering and Technology Import/Export Corp -- and a Hong Kong company, Cheong Yee Limited. Also five Chinese citizens were penalized.
